title: VPC Private Deploy: offline-bootstrap & operator-upgrade acceptance criteria (egress-minimal strategy)
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Purpose: Define concrete requirements and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments that perform offline (airgapped or egress-minimal) bootstrap and operator-based control-plane upgrades. The goal is to allow customers with strict network egress constraints to safely install and upgrade Redwood Private while preserving operator safety, artifact provenance (image signatures and checksums), and deterministic rollback. This ticket captures the product requirements, operational constraints, scope decisions, success metrics, and test plans needed for the upcoming release.

Background: Several enterprise customers require zero or tightly controlled egress during initial bootstrap and during operator or control-plane upgrades. Existing work covers offline image distribution and mirror strategies, but customers require a documented, automated operator upgrade pathway that: (1) validates artifact provenance without outbound calls, (2) provides staged canaries and rollback hooks, (3) supports KMS/HSM rotation during upgrades, and (4) integrates with on-prem mirrors or physical media fallback.

Goals:
- Provide an operator upgrade flow that completes end-to-end without internet access when mirrored artifacts are present locally.
- Define minimal egress exceptions required for optional telemetry and emergency fetches; prefer explicit allowlists and one-time signed artifact pulls.
- Ensure upgrades are provably repeatable and verifiable via checksums and signature verification anchored to customer KMS or airgapped signing keys.
- Provide clear observability and contingency playbooks (canary metrics, operator safe-mode, automated rollback triggers).

Out of scope: full redesign of Kubernetes operators; changes to customer network appliances; optional managed-bastion provisioning automation (will be separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Offline bootstrap completes using local artifact mirror with no outbound network egress when mirror manifest and image bundles are present; bootstrap runbook demonstrates success in an isolated lab environment.

AC-2: Operator upgrade can be executed from a staged bundle (OCI tar or mirror registry) and performs preflight checksum and signature verification using a customer-provided public key or KMS-wrapped signing key; if verification fails, the upgrade aborts and operator enters 'paused' safe-mode.

AC-3: Upgrade canary path: upgrades applied to a single control-plane replica (or single-zone subset) and automated health-checks run for at least 10 minutes; if critical health or latency regressions exceed configured thresholds, rollout is stopped and a rollback is initiated.

AC-4: Zero-egress option: documented bootstrap and upgrade mode that requires no network egress for artifact verification or image pulling. This mode must include instructions for physical media ingestion or local registry mirroring and produce identical runtime manifests as the standard flow.

AC-5: Minimal-egress option: when customer allows minimal outbound connectivity, the system requires a single short-lived TLS connection to a signed artifact endpoint and then performs an offline verification; the required outbound hosts and ports are documented and limited to a single IP/hostname list.

AC-6: KMS/HSM rotation during upgrade: operator must support a maintenance step to rotate keys (KMS/HSM) with a documented rollback plan; rotation should not require internet egress if keys and rotation metadata are supplied via mirror.

AC-7: Artifact provenance proof: every upgrade bundle must include an immutable manifest with SHA256 checksums and a detached signature; the operator validates both and writes verification results to the local audit log accessible via Console telemetry export (or local file in airgapped installs).

AC-8: Automated rollback criteria: rollback is triggered if (a) any critical pod enters CrashLoopBackOff during the canary window, (b) request p50 latency regression > 2x from baseline for more than 3 consecutive minutes, or (c) >1% error rate increase for 5 minutes for critical API routes. Rollback completes to previous image set and writes an incident event to the audit log.

AC-9: Observability without egress: essential telemetry (upgrade progress, verification results, health checks) is captured and persisted locally for at least 30 days and available through the private Console or exported to a customer-provided syslog/ELK collector; documentation includes instructions for offline log retrieval.

AC-10: Test harness: automated integration tests that simulate (1) full offline bootstrap from local mirror, (2) staged operator upgrade with signature mismatch, (3) canary regression detection and rollback, and (4) KMS rotation without egress. Tests must be runnable in CI constrained-network mode.
AC-11: Security approval: security review completed and signed-off with documented threat model updates for the offline and minimal-egress upgrade paths.
notes_progress: 2025-01-10: Ticket created to consolidate multiple customer asks into a single acceptance-criteria driven PRD. Initial scoping call with Eng and Security scheduled.

2025-01-12: Eng proposal v1 received (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-operator/pull/674). Proposal outlines operator 'safe-mode' and detached-signature verification. Eng flagged complexity around KMS adapter in airgapped mode.

2025-01-14: Security reviewed the draft and requested explicit handling for signature key bootstrapping; recommended support for customer-supplied signing bundle and HSM-wrapped keys (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/Offline+Signing+Design).

2025-01-16: Decided to support two modes: 'zero-egress' (no external calls) and 'minimal-egress' (documented one-time fetch). Trade-off: zero-egress increases operator complexity and requires customers to provide mirrored registry or physical media; minimal-egress reduces operator changes but requires allowlist approvals.
2025-01-18: Added explicit acceptance criteria for KMS/HSM rotation and local audit log retention. Eng to deliver integration tests by 2025-01-30 (ENG-8421).
2025-01-22: Customer pilot candidate list prepared; signed NDAs and support windows aligned for two financial customers. Operational runbook draft attached.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Customers fail to produce correct mirror artifacts or signatures. Mitigation: provide a validator tool that runs locally and reports mismatches before operator install.

Risk: Operator complexity leads to upgrade deadlocks in rare states. Mitigation: implement operator 'safe-mode' with manual override and a clear rollback CLI endpoint; include canned playbooks for SREs.
Risk: KMS integration requires cloud access. Mitigation: support HSM-supplied wrapped keys or an offline key injection path documented in the runbook.
Risk: Observability gaps in zero-egress installs. Mitigation: require local retention of upgrade artefacts and a standardized export format for offline review.
test_plan: 1) Lab test: Perform full offline bootstrap in isolated VLAN using a pre-populated local registry mirror. Validate service readiness and run smoke tests.
2) Signature negative test: Attempt upgrade with intentionally corrupted detached signature; operator must abort and mark upgrade as failed.
3) Canary rollback test: Introduce a performance regression on canary node and assert automatic rollback triggers within configured thresholds.
4) KMS rotation test: Perform a rotation using a mirrored rotation bundle and validate service continuity and audit events.
5) Telemetry export test: Verify local audit logs can be exported and consumed by customer ELK without egress.
scope_changes: Original scope included only offline bootstrap; added operator upgrade acceptance criteria after customer feedback (scope increase approved on 2025-01-14).
Added explicit KMS/HSM rotation support requirement (requested by Security).
Excluded: automated bastion provisioning and network appliance integration (will be separate tickets).
